title: Retry-safe VCF Operations custom-group reconciler derived from the 9.1 OpenAPI spec
prompt:
Our deploy pipeline needs a reconcile step against VCF Operations in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 -- the Operations Suite API itself, not Log Management. The step has to guarantee that a named custom group exists with a given membership rule, and because the pipeline retries steps, running it twice must converge on the same group rather than leaving two behind or blowing up. The API has no upsert for custom groups, so retry safety has to come out of how you sequence the calls that do exist.

Nobody here has written against this API before, so start by pinning down the wire protocol from the published OpenAPI specification -- `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository on GitHub, at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. Work from that file, not from a rendered documentation page; retrieve and read it. Record what you find in `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json`, then implement `src/main/java/com/vmware/vcfops/VcfOperationsClient.java` against it. The specification names the `Authorization` header but does not encode the session-token value prefix; for VCF Operations 9.1, use `OpsToken <token>` as required by the client constraints below.

`README.md` has the required shape of both JSON documents and the constraints on the client (single file, JDK only, exact wire shape, unset optional fields omitted rather than sent empty). `harness/TestMain.java` compiles against the client's public surface, so keep that surface as the stub declares it. `bash harness/run_tests.sh` runs the client against a loopback mock pinned to your contract and prints the captured request log; `bash verification/run.sh` runs the full check. `README.md`, `harness/`, and `verification/` are protected fixtures: read and run them, but do not edit them.
network_rationale: the agent must retrieve the pinned OpenAPI specification from github.com; verification itself is loopback-only and contacts no VMware endpoint
